exact_statement: (A) MeanRank, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026/build/sections/setup.tex:115-121, Lemma \label{setup:local-factors} (compiled Lemma 2.2), verbatim: 'For \(F\in\mathcal F\) and admissible \(d\), L_{F^{(d)}}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_F(n)\chi_d(n)n^{-s}, q_{F^{(d)}}=q_F|d|^2, \chi_d(n)=(d/n). Here the symbol is the Kronecker symbol and d=1 has the untwisted convention. For an arbitrary signed squarefree b, the same good-prime twisting rule holds at primes outside S: the local trace is multiplied by (b/p) when p\nmid b, and the local factor is one when p\mid b.' Hypotheses (setup.tex:69-82): S={p : p | 2 q_E}, Q_S=prod_{p in S} p; F ranges over the finite set of twists of E by signed squarefree products of primes of S; d is 'admissible' iff d = 1 (mod 4) and (d,Q_S)=1. Proof (setup.tex:123-145): Tate module of a quadratic twist = original tensor quadratic character; admissible d is an odd fundamental discriminant, unramified at S; at p | d the representation of F is unramified, the character tamely ramified, tensor product has no inertia invariants, Swan conductor 0, Artin exponent 2. Cites arXiv 1410.1039v1 (Dokchitser-Anni, 'l-adic representations and their associated invariants', references.bib:200-206) for Artin-conductor definitions. (B) Goldfeld2, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/03-heegner.tex:658-676, Lemma \label{lem:h:central-valuation} [Central determinant valuation] (compiled Lemma 13.5): 'For a simple-zero instance, v(u(0)) = 2j(P_c(e)) - length Sha(E^{(e)}/K)[2^infty] - sum_{q|c} sum_{v|q} t_v + O_E(1), t_v = dim_{F_2} E[2]^{Fr_v}. Furthermore length Sha(E^{(e)}/K)[2^infty] + sum_{q|c}sum_{v|q} t_v = s(e)+s(ek)+sum_{q|k} t_q + 2 sum_{q|c} t_q + O_E(1).' Inside its proof (03-heegner.tex:723-736), verbatim: 'The remaining terms are the Tamagawa numbers. A ramified quadratic twist of good reduction at an odd prime q has type I_0^* and component number one plus the number of roots of its reduced auxiliary cubic \citep[Theorem~4.1, Table~4 and proof, Case~3]{BarriosEtAl2025}. To identify this number, write a good integral model as y^2=f(x), retaining the quadratic term, and the twisting parameter as d=\pi u. The auxiliary cubic is \bar u^3\bar f(T/\bar u); it is separable and its roots correspond to the nonzero rational two-torsion points. Thus the component number is \#E[2]^{Fr_q} and its 2-valuation is t_q. This argument also applies in residue characteristic 3.' (BarriosEtAl2025 = Barrios, Roy, Sahajpal, Tallana, Tobin, Wiersema, 'Local data of elliptic curves under quadratic twist', Res. Number Theory 11 (2025), art. 75, doi 10.1007/s40993-025-00650-w; references.bib:710-718.) The lemma itself (simple-zero instance over a Heegner field, ultrafilter-uniform constants) is NOT used here; only the quoted classical Tamagawa sentence is. (C) Goldfeld2, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/01-preliminaries.tex:171-179, Lemma \label{pr:finite-descent} [Finite descent and corank] (compiled Lemma 2.4), verbatim: 'Let F be the quotient of \Sha(E/\Q)[2^\infty] by its maximal divisible subgroup. Then d_2(E)=c_2(E)+\dim_{\F_2}F[2], \dim_{\F_2}F[2] is even. Thus d_2(E)\in\{0,1\} implies c_2(E)=d_2(E) and F=0.' Definitions: d_2(E)=dim_{F_2} Sel_2(E/Q) - dim_{F_2} E(Q)[2] (00-introduction.tex:58); c_2(E)=corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty}(E/Q) with c_2(A)=r(A)+corank Sha(A/Q)[2^infty] (Lemma pr:ranks, 01-preliminaries.tex:12-25). Proof (01-preliminaries.tex:181-198): Kummer sequence at n=1 gives d_2=r+dim Sha[2]; divisible part splits off with 2-torsion dimension = corank; Cassels-Tate pairing on F is perfect and alternating (cites Milne ADT Ch. I Remark 6.10(b), Thm 6.13(a)); alternating finite 2-group has even 2-rank. Corollary \label{cor:finite-descent} (00-introduction.tex:61-67): 'If d_2(E) in {0,1}, then a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)=d_2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite, Sha(E/Q)[2^infty]=0' -- its a(E) part depends on the manuscript's unrefereed 2-converse Theorem 1.1 and is NOT used here. (D) Pointwise2, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/build/sections/preliminaries.tex:13-41, Lemma \label{pr:ranks} [The three ranks]: exact sequence 0 -> A(Q) tensor Q_2/Z_2 -> Sel_{2^infty}(A/Q) -> Sha(A/Q)[2^infty] -> 0, s_2(A)=r(A)+corank Sha(A/Q)[2^infty]; 'If a(A) in {0,1}, then r(A)=a(A) and the whole group Sha(A/Q) is finite. In that case s_2(A)=a(A)' (cites Gross-Zagier 1986, Kolyvagin 1990, Skinner 2020 Sec. 1); preliminaries.tex:48-78 Lemma pr:invariance: (-1)^{s_2(A)}=epsilon(A) (Monsky 1996; Dokchitser-Dokchitser 2010 Thm 1.4/4.19), isogeny invariance, s_2(A/K)=s_2(A/Q)+s_2(A^{(k)}/Q). All classical.

The check is therefore of the DERIVED local data, prime by prime, against the seed record (SEED_CONTEXT.md lines 20-27, 36-41), redone here in pure Python (no PARI/Sage available). Hence q_{E^{-7}} = 49 N = 2^3*3*7^2*2243*4547^2*5843 = 318656212624190616; the SEED_CONTEXT.md line 36 record 'conductor N, same bad primes' is WRONG (7 does not divide N, checked; the twist by Q(sqrt-7) is ramified exactly at 7). deduction_for_seed: Chain 1 (conductor and local data; no manuscript needed): seed data (N, reduction types, a_p, c_p at 2,3,2243,4547,5843; 7 does not divide N) + classical twisting facts (quadratic twist by a p-adic square is a Q_p-isomorphism; unramified nontrivial twist of multiplicative reduction swaps split/nonsplit and keeps I_n; ramified twist of good reduction at odd p is I_0^* with c = 1 + #roots of the auxiliary cubic = #E[2](F_p), Tate's algorithm step 6 / Silverman ATAEC IV.9 Table 4.1; conductor exponent 2 at a tamely ramified twist prime) => N(E^{-7}) = 49N, bad primes {2,3,7,2243,4547,5843}, c(E^{-7}) = (2,2,2,1,2,2), prod c = 32, E^{-7}(Q)_tors = Z/2, global minimal model y^2 = x^3+159145x^2+5207351716x. MeanRank Lemma 2.2 and the Goldfeld2 sentence merely restate the classical facts; they are not load-bearing. Chain 2 (BSD-predicted order, a target, NOT a theorem): recorded L(E^{-7},1) in [9.054319, 9.054421] (PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED per SEED_CONTEXT.md line 37; the underlying record is not in reference/ -- thm:d7 is cited there but not present) + Omega_{E^{-7}} = 0.02309788253231444... (computed here, 40-digit AGM) + prod c = 32 + #tors = 2 => Q_{E^{-7}} := L(E^{-7},1) #tors^2 / (Omega prod c) in [48.99972, 49.00028]. Hence, IF BSD holds for E^{-7} (which is NOT assumed anywhere else), #Sha(E^{-7}/Q) = 49 = 7^2 and Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[p^infty] = 0 for every p != 7, including p=2, 3, 2243, 4547, 5843 and all good p. This is exactly the quantity the ExactBSD manuscript (Thm 1.1, Prop 10.4) and TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 claim to certify for E^{-7} at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT; the lab now has the number those claims would have to reproduce. Consistency evidence (not proof): Q is within 3e-4 of a perfect square integer; with c_7=4 instead of 2 the quotient would be 24.5 (non-integer) and with prod c = 16 it would be 98 (non-square), so the derived local data and the recorded L-value (which must have been computed with conductor 49N, not N, for the functional equation to hold) are mutually consistent to 5 significant figures. Chain 3 (unconditional 2-part, after a lab computation): L(E^{-7},1) != 0 + Gross-Zagier 1986 / Kolyvagin 1990 (published) => rank E^{-7}(Q)=0 and Sha(E^{-7}/Q) finite, so Sha(E^{-7})[2^infty] = F (its finite quotient) and corank 0. Kummer sequence at 2 (published, elementary): dim_{F_2} Sel_2(E^{-7}/Q) = rank + dim E^{-7}(Q)[2] + dim Sha(E^{-7})[2] = 0 + 1 + dim Sha[2]. Cassels-Tate alternating pairing on the finite group Sha(E^{-7})[2^infty] (Cassels 1962; Milne ADT I.6.10(b)/6.13(a), published) => dim Sha[2] even, so dim Sel_2 is odd, in {1,3,...}. A 2-isogeny descent on E^{-7} (phi: E^{-7} -> E' with kernel (0,0), E': y^2 = x^3 - 318290 x^2 + 4497724161 x, bad primes of E' = {2,3,7,2243,4547}) gives the phi- and phi-hat-Selmer groups S^phi subset {+-1}x<2,7,4547,5843> (32 candidates) and S^phihat subset {+-1}x<3,7,2243,4547> (32 candidates), each by local solubility of d w^2 = d^2 + a d z^2 + b z^4 at the places 2,3,7,2243,4547,5843,infinity; then dim Sel_2(E^{-7}) <= dim S^phi + dim S^phihat - 1 (the -1 is E'(Q)[phihat]/phi(E^{-7}(Q)[2]) = Z/2; the omitted term Sha(E')[phihat]/phi(Sha[2]) is >= 0). If the bound is 1 then Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[2] = 0, hence Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[2^infty] = 0 at grade PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED using only published inputs. If the bound is 3 or more, a full 2-descent (or Cassels-Tate refinement) is needed; dim Sel_2 = 3 would contradict the BSD prediction 49 and would signal an error in the L-value, the local data or the descent. No part of chains 1-3 uses any OAI manuscript as an input; the manuscripts only flagged the conductor error and suggested the descent.

risks: (1) The L-value provenance: SEED_CONTEXT.md records conductor N for E^{-7}; if the recorded interval had been computed with the wrong conductor the functional-equation-based evaluation would be wrong. The fact that Q lands on 49.0000 +- 0.0003 makes this unlikely, but the lab must locate the original computation (thm:d7) and confirm 49N was used before relying on either the interval or the prediction. (2) Period normalization: Omega over both real components with the Neron differential of the global minimal twist model; if the lab's L-value or any later comparison uses a one-component period or a non-minimal model the quotient changes by 2 or by 7-powers. The twist model minimality was checked only by v_p(Delta')<12 at every p (sufficient). (3) The 2-isogeny descent gives an upper bound on dim Sel_2; only the value 1 closes the 2-part. Pure-Python local-solubility code is error-prone (especially at p=2 with I1* reduction and at the twisted prime 7); the lab should cross-check at least one Selmer element against an explicit global point/cover and should test the code on a curve with known Sel_2 (e.g. y^2=x^3-x). (4) Goldfeld2's Tamagawa sentence says 'component number one plus the number of roots of its reduced auxiliary cubic ... Thus the component number is #E[2]^{Fr_q}' and 'This argument also applies in residue characteristic 3': the identification of auxiliary-cubic roots with rational 2-torsion assumes the good model is in the form y^2=f(x) (p odd), fine at q=7; it is not needed in characteristic 3 here (3 is multiplicative for E). Not load-bearing. (5) The predicted #Sha(E^{-7}) = 49 is conjectural; a nontrivial predicted 7-part means the twist certificate B is predicted nonzero at p=7, which the lab's frozen route already excludes (p not dividing 7N) but which must not be forgotten if 7 is ever treated as a good prime of E (7 IS good for E: a_7=-2, ordinary). (6) MeanRank's cited reference DokchitserAnni2014 (arXiv 1410.1039v1) is cited only for definitions; the lemma is classical, no risk. (7) #E^{-7}(Q)_tors = 2 was checked by a gcd of point counts at 11 good primes and the Z/4 test; adequate but should be re-run by the lab.
